processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: A 100 g alloy ingot was prepared by melting 99.99% pure iron, 99.9% pure manganese, 99.9% pure aluminum, 99.9% pure chromium and 99.8% high-purity graphite. This alloy is the 3Cr composition (Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr).

processing_steps_notes.value: The metal ingot was remelted by induction melting and poured into a copper mold rotating at 600 rpm; as-cast steel strips with size 80 mm × 60 mm × 2.5 mm were obtained.

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h was chosen because it promotes precipitation of κ-carbides without coarsening, giving better comprehensive mechanical properties. These strips are referred as 'annealed steel strips'.

structures.overall_structure: Austenite-based duplex structure: γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed within it. Nano-scale κ-carbides are precipitated in the γ-austenite and an ordered DO3 phase forms in the δ-ferrite. Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h collapses the 43.5–45.0° double peak into a single peak, i.e. almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase.

precipitates.distribution: Precipitated in γ-austenite; dark-field (001) images show a clearly lower particle density than in the annealed 0Cr strip (7%/8 nm). Annealing at 600 °C promotes precipitation and growth of κ-carbides.

microstructure_list.region: irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed in the γ-austenite matrix

phases_present.crystal_structure: body centered cubic, space group Fm3m, a = 0.565 nm
phases_present.morphology: ordered phase within δ-ferrite (XRD: 43.5–45.0° double peak collapses to a single peak on annealing; single-peak intensity increases with Cr content)

defect_interactions.qualitative_or_quantitative_description: Nano-scale κ-carbides act as reinforcing phases hindering dislocation glide by providing an energy barrier; the decrease of κ-carbides caused by Cr addition contributes to the formation of dislocations and increases the density of the slip bands. Glide-plane softening occurs when dislocations shear the short-range-ordered κ-carbides.

interfaces.slip_behavior: For the annealed strips the strain hardening rate is lower than that of the corresponding as-cast strips. A nearly stable platform is observed in the strain hardening rate curve of the annealed 3Cr steel strip, in contrast to the clear double-hump feature of the annealed 0Cr strip, attributed to the lower number of nano-scale κ-carbides at the early strain stage. Slip bands form at the early strain stage and microbands at the final strain stage (double hardening).
interfaces.phase_evolution: Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h changes the 43.5–45.0° double peak into a single peak, indicating almost all the ferrite transforms into the ordered DO3 phase; the single-peak intensity increases with Cr content in the annealed strips, indicating the DO3 content does increase.
interfaces.interface_notes: Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h promotes precipitation and growth of κ-carbides (annealed 0Cr: 7% and 8 nm; annealed 3Cr: 4% and 4 nm), increasing yield strength. Cr addition expands the solid solubility of Al and C, reducing the driving force for κ-carbide formation, so higher Cr gives less κ-carbide precipitation.

measurement_conditions.specimen_geometry: gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm
measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile tests performed at least 3 times by an MTS Criterion 44 Mechanical Property Tester

tensile_properties.stress_strain_curves: Engineering stress-strain curve of the annealed 3Cr strip (Fig. 3b) rises gradually past 1000 MPa to ~33–36% strain; the annealed strips show lower strain hardening rate than the as-cast strips (Fig. 3d).
strain_hardening_rate: A nearly stable platform is observed in the strain hardening rate curve of the annealed 3Cr steel strip (no distinct hump), unlike the annealed 0Cr strip which shows a clear double hump.

comparative_performance.improvement_percentage: Annealing increased the yield strength of the 3Cr steel strip by 277 MPa (as-cast 642 MPa → annealed 919 MPa)

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Rigaku, D/Max-2200, Cu target operated at 40 kV and 40 mA, graphite monochromator, λ = 0.154056 nm
characterization_methods.purpose: Phase identification of the as-cast and annealed steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed strips show the 43.5–45.0° double peak collapsed into a single peak; the single-peak intensity increases from 0Cr to 6Cr, indicating the ordered DO3 content increases with Cr content.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: after mechanical polishing and etching (3.3 vol.% nitric acid, 3.3 vol.% acetic acid, 0.1 vol.% hydrofluoric acid; etching time 3 s); photographs taken 0.5 mm from the strip surface along the thickness direction; phase fraction from ten positions using Image-Pro Plus
characterization_methods.purpose: Characterise microstructure and measure δ-ferrite volume fraction
characterization_methods.key_findings: Irregularly shaped δ-ferrite distributed in the γ-austenite matrix; annealed 3Cr shows multiple blocky δ-ferrite particles. δ-ferrite volume fraction of the annealed 3Cr strip is 14%.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Specimens prepared by twin-jet electrolytic polishing at −30 °C and 30 V, with a mixed solution of 10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol; BF images and SADP (dark-field from (001) superlattice reflection)
characterization_methods.purpose: Elucidate the nano-scale precipitated κ-carbide phase in the annealed steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Superlattice reflection spots appear in the SADP along [110] from γ-austenite; DF images using (001) show a large number of nano-scale κ-carbides in the annealed strips. The annealed 3Cr strip has a κ-carbide volume fraction of 4% and average size 4 nm (lower density than annealed 0Cr).

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; constant strain rate 2.5 × 10^-4 s^-1; per GB/T-228.1-2010; gage width 4 mm, gage length 12 mm; at least 3 tests
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the mechanical properties of the strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Annealed 3Cr: YS 919 ± 5 MPa, UTS 1033 ± 10 MPa, TE 33 ± 4 % (Table 2); annealing raises YS by 277 MPa.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: AccuPyc II 1340 Gas Displacement Density Analyzer
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure the average density of the steel strips
characterization_methods.key_findings: Measured average density of the 3Cr steel strip is 6.69 g/cm3.

unmapped_findings: The product of ultimate tensile strength and total elongation (UTS × TE) for the annealed 3Cr steel strip is 34.1 GPa % (Table 2).
Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h increases the δ-ferrite volume fraction of the 3Cr strip from 12% (as-cast) to 14% (annealed).

The strain hardening rate curve of the annealed 3Cr steel strip shows a nearly stable platform, which is attributed to the small number of nano-scale κ-carbides (from the Cr addition) giving a higher early-stage strain hardening rate than the microband-hardening level.

Annealing at 600 °C for 3 h promotes the precipitation and growth of κ-carbides in the strips, which increases the yield strength; the higher the Cr content, the less the κ-carbide precipitation because Cr expands the solid solubility of Al and C.
For the annealed Cr-containing strips the strain hardening rate is lower than that of the corresponding as-cast strips (Fig. 3).

A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism is proposed for the strain hardening of these low-density steel strips: slip bands act at the early strain stage and microbands at the final strain stage.
